slides.headline: Google just redrew the search box — after 25 years
slides.body: Gemini 3.5 Flash is now the default for everyone, globally.

slides.headline: Search hasn't fundamentally changed since 1998
slides.body: The text box and ten blue links have outlasted every attempt to replace them. Voice search, rich snippets, Knowledge Graph, featured snippets — each iteration kept the same basic contract: you type a query, Google returns a ranked list. The interface survived because it was fast, predictable, and universal. What Google announced at I/O 2026 is the first change to that contract that does not merely add a layer on top of the box.

slides.headline: AI Mode goes global; the search box becomes an agent launchpad
slides.body: Google made Gemini 3.5 Flash the default model inside AI Mode and rolled it out globally on May 19. Alongside that, Google revealed a redesigned search entry point described as the biggest change to the search interface in over 25 years. Users can now create and manage multiple AI agents directly inside Search — turning the box from a query input into a persistent task surface. The change affects billions of daily active users immediately.

slides.headline: The default model change is the distribution moat
slides.body: Making Gemini 3.5 Flash the global default for AI Mode is not a product launch — it is a distribution event. Every person who opens Google Search now interacts with Gemini whether or not they chose to. That scale of default placement is something no standalone AI product, including ChatGPT, can replicate without a search engine behind it. Google is using its existing moat to make the AI transition nearly frictionless for its existing user base.

slides.headline: Agents inside Search redefine what 'search intent' means
slides.body: Letting users build and manage agents inside the search interface collapses the distinction between querying and doing. Right now, search answers questions. With persistent agents embedded in Search, the same interface can book a restaurant, monitor a price, or draft a reply — without the user leaving the box. That shift from 'find information' to 'accomplish tasks' rewrites the value proposition of Search and, by extension, the entire advertising model that sits on top of it.

items.body: The ad model for 'accomplish this task' looks nothing like cost-per-click — that transition is the defining business story of 2026-2027.
